previousDefinition.question: Is there a centering pass for this study?
previousDefinition.target: Identify the qualifying setup transfer after an ordinary deep receiving pull. The binary label controls the study’s first-throw deduction; it does not inventory every pass that physically centers the disc.
previousDefinition.centeringPass: A completed setup transfer after an ordinary in-bounds pull received near the receiving team’s own goal-line or end-zone area, caught or picked up. The intended receiver is immediately available, mostly stationary and uncontested. Small adjustments solely to catch the disc are allowed. The thrower does not change targets because of coverage, and the receiver does not move to evade either defender. A qualifying transfer need not move toward the middle. The usual deep starting area is descriptive; no new numerical location cutoff is adopted.
previousDefinition.noCenteringPass: No centering pass if the thrower visibly abandons the initial intended transfer because of defensive coverage and selects another receiver, even if the eventual receiver is stationary and the pass is easy. No centering pass if the receiver must cut, sprint, evade, or change direction to get open around either defender. A reset after looking downfield, an under, a huck, or an incomplete opening transfer also remains no centering pass. For the study label, a sideline-start transfer also receives No centering pass, even if it physically centers the disc immediately and uncontested. Its exclusion from the deduction is based on restart context, not on a claim that no centering action happened.
previousDefinition.cannotTell: Use Cannot tell when the footage or record alignment does not establish the opening transfer, receiver movement, or a relevant change of target. Do not infer an unseen first read, defensive coverage or tactical intent from the final pass coordinates.
previousDefinition.timing: Immediate describes the visible, uninterrupted initial transfer, not a fixed number of seconds. Do not impose a timing cutoff or infer a blocked first option from recorded event timestamp gaps.
previousDefinition.counting: Subtract exactly one opening throw only for a confirmed, completed centering transfer. Keep every attempted throw, including interceptions and drops, when no such transfer was completed. A one-throw Callahan possession remains one attempt, zero completed passes and a turnover; it must not become a zero-throw possession or be removed. Subsequent possessions receive no deduction. Keep the original starting coordinates.
previousDefinition.restartRules: Sideline starts, including out-of-bounds rollers and the previously grouped in-bounds sideline starts, are outside the ordinary pull-setup deduction. Keep the first throw even if a quick pickup creates an uncontested centering transfer. The exact-brick rule and preserved film-coordinate conflicts remain unchanged. A back-end-line restart remains a separate context; this example does not establish an additional rule for every rolling pull.
previousDefinition.compatibility: Keep setup1 and attack1 as existing storage codes. attack1 now displays as No centering pass; it does not imply an immediate, aggressive or downfield throw.
previousDefinition.automaticLabels: Pass endpoints and recorded timestamp gaps do not establish receiver evasion, a blocked first option or a change of read. Keep geometry predictions as frozen development evidence; do not apply this definition or league-wide deductions from coordinates alone.
previousDefinition.attemptAndOutcome: Where visible, preserve intended setup separately from completion. The user did not settle the precise intended pass in the Houston Callahan example; do not infer intent from its outcome.
previousDefinition.interpretationLimit: Completed-centering status depends on the result of the first throw. It is suitable for the user-defined completed-transfer count adjustment, but comparing scoring or huck success between these label groups cannot by itself establish a difference in tactical preference. Report all-attempt results alongside adjusted counts; failed opening throws stay in the denominator.
previousDefinition.versioning: Preserve physical observations separately from study eligibility and keep earlier definitions and labels. Earlier positive centering labels require checking against the ordinary-pull setup scope, receiver-movement and first-option criteria before use under the current definition. Historical adjusted comparisons and classifier evaluations remain unrevalidated.

backEndlineRuleSource.interpretation: A pull landing in bounds and rolling out the back is put into play on the back line. This rule does not say whether the next pass is centering.

sidelineStartGroup.label: Sideline start
sidelineStartGroup.scope: Opening receiving possessions that begin at or near a sideline after the pull, including an in-bounds pull and a roller that exits at the sideline.
sidelineStartGroup.source: User instruction in chat, November 13, 2026: group sideline opening possessions together even when the pull stays in bounds.
sidelineStartGroup.counting: Keep the first throw; sideline starts do not receive the study’s centering deduction even when a centering transfer occurs.

contexts.sideline: Pull rolls out of bounds on the sideline (existing saved code).
contexts.sideline_inbounds: Pull stays in bounds near the sideline (caught or picked up).

sidelineStartGroup.evidence: Reviewer identifies the start from film. Preserve pull outcome separately from the shared sideline-start group.
sidelineStartGroup.coordinatePolicy: Do not assign this group from wide coordinates alone until near the sideline is operationally defined and checked against film.
sidelineStartGroup.intentPolicy: Intent to pin the receiving team is a possible explanation; it is not required or inferred by the label.
sidelineStartGroup.conflictPolicy: Preserve earlier labels and observations; flag a setup1 study label for review against the sideline scope. An observed centering action with an attack1 study label is not a conflict.
scopeExclusions: A later possession that starts on the sideline is not a pull-opening sideline start.
A back-end-line start remains a separate context.

fieldSemantics.decision: setup1 means a qualifying centering pass for this study; attack1 means no qualifying centering pass. It does not assert that the pass was aggressive or that the disc never moved toward the middle.
fieldSemantics.hasOpeningCenteringPass: Legacy Boolean for the qualifying study label.
fieldSemantics.completedCenteringPass: Legacy Boolean for a completed qualifying transfer; not a comprehensive observation of physical centering.
fieldSemantics.qualifyingCenteringPass: Explicit Boolean for the study’s eligible centering transfer.
fieldSemantics.observedCenteringPass: Optional independent film observation. Set only when explicitly established; missing means not separately annotated, not false.
